mount.note: MEASURED, not fitted. pitch_deg 23.8 comes from the encoder and the level frames: with the head level by eye the tilt servo reads 2068 ticks and the picture is 1.0 deg down (+-1.5), and the reference pose sits 2311 - 2068 = 243 ticks further down at 360/4096 deg a tick, which is 23.8 (scratch/neck_tilt_scale.txt, four still frames of one room, 2026-09-12). z_m 1.203 is the tape: floor to tilt axis 1.134 m (reference.axis_z_m in config/neck.json) plus the lens 0.086 m above it and 0.025 m in front, turned down by that pitch. Both replace the 26.0 / 1.23 the lidar-beam fit of 2026-09-10 voted for (scratch/depth_fit_models.py), which was owed a repeat anyway: its beams were projected at a lidar mount the tape corrected on 2026-09-12.

The NECK's link, exactly the overview camera's measured mount (z_m 1.203, pitch_deg 23.8: the tape and the encoder, 2026-09-12), because the module is taped onto that webcam and the board publishes base_link -> camera_link from the neck's encoders either way. Where the module's LEFT eye sits and looks relative to that link is the 'eye' block below — never folded into this one, so the neck's frame means the same thing under every head.

eye.note: The rectified LEFT eye in camera_link's axes (x forward, y left, z up), composed into camera_link -> camera_optical. MEASURED 2026-09-30 at the sticker door (2.0 m by lidar), module re-taped flat on the webcam that day, with the eye-to-eye rotation refitted the same evening (config/stereo_calibration.json): two runs of scratch/stereo/mount_from_floor_and_door.py, floor height 1.197/1.210 m where the link says 1.203 (so z 0), pitch -2.44/-2.25, roll +1.9/+1.5, yaw by the door-plane solver -3.0/-1.3 but REFUTED by a pixelwise scan against the lidar at a room corner (2 m, six SGBM frames, 20 scans, the node's own frame composition): the error has its minimum at yaw +3.6 (5.6 %; -2 gives 9.8 %), the same sign the fan tool gave at the door (+4.1), so +3.6; door by stereo 2.025/1.974 m against the lidar's 2.009. Before (2026-09-21, a chip under the tape lifted one side): {"x_m": -0.011, "y_m": 0.0305, "z_m": 0.025, "roll_deg": -3.7, "pitch_deg": -5.6, "yaw_deg": 4.3}. The module is taped, so a knock changes these: the depth node's law line (a 1.00) is the alarm. y_m is NOT measured: half the calibrated 61 mm baseline to the left, assuming the module is centred on the webcam's lens.

exposure.note: What the board's camera service sets with v4l2-ctl before ustreamer starts (pepin.camera_controls, board/pepin-camera.service ExecStartPre; ustreamer itself changes no exposure). auto: the camera's own defaults, as it ran before this block existed. manual: exposure_ms fixed (the control counts 100 us) and gain when not null (the camera's raw units; ros/exposure.sh shows its range). capped: auto, never longer than exposure_ms where the camera offers shutter priority, else one frame period (it says which). Values the camera does not offer are refused, never clamped. Try one live, nothing restarted: ros/exposure.sh show | auto | manual MS [GAIN] | capped MS; then write it here, copy this file to /opt/pepin/config/ and restart pepin-camera. With a manual exposure set every gated node's gate_exposure_s to it (ros/gaze_gate.sh gate_exposure_s SECONDS). Unmeasured: the module's control set (read it with ros/exposure.sh show), its auto exposure indoors, and the blur at a known head rate.

net.note: RAFT-Stereo, the alternative matcher behind the depth node's live stereo_matcher flag (default sgbm). It runs on the laptop's GPU in a native process, NOT in the container (pepin.stereo_host, ros/depth_host.sh stereo): Docker on macOS cannot see Metal, where the same forward pass is 91 ms against about 3 fps on the container's CPU. weights is the checkpoint, relative to the repo root; models/ is gitignored, so an empty path simply means this machine has no checkpoint and the flag cannot be turned on. realtime MEASURED better than middlebury on this rig (5264 airborne phantoms against 42138 over the lamp's reflection on the parquet, and 89 ms a pair against 437), and iters 7 is that architecture's own trained count. gate puts the SGBM texture gate over the network's dense output; off, because the network is not confidently wrong on blank wall the way SGBM is and a texture gate would throw away exactly the floor the network wins. Measured 2026-09-22 through this path (scratch/stereo_net/host_smoke.py); the whole table, and what did NOT reproduce from the earlier note, are in pepin.stereo_host.

stereo.notes: The stereo head: ONE side-by-side MJPEG frame of 1600x600 from ustreamer on the board (rig.frame_width x rig.frame_height), cut into two 800x600 eyes by pepin.stereo.SideBySide. width/height are ONE EYE — the picture every consumer of /camera/image sees — while the frame on the wire is twice as wide. upside_down is MEASURED on a real frame: the module is taped upside down, so each half is turned 180 deg and the halves trade places, and only then is the disparity of near objects positive. hfov_deg 94.0 and baseline_m_nominal 0.063 are the VENDOR's numbers, the nominal pinhole pepin.camera.optics falls back to while there is no calibration; both are replaced by config/stereo_calibration.json the moment it exists (the rectified pinhole and the baseline come from there, never from here). This block has no intrinsics of its own: calibrated means that file exists and loads. STAMPS: ustreamer's X-Timestamp is the SEND time, 1-68 ms after the V4L2 capture and bimodal (~1-5 or ~50 ms), measured 2026-10-02 (scratch/head_imu/ustreamer_stamps.py); the capture stamp (X-UStreamer-Grab-Time beside X-UStreamer-Send-Time) comes only with ?extra_headers=1 on the stream URL, which is why it is there; camera_stream's camera_stamp flag picks which one the frames carry.

head_imu.method: 2026-10-04: rotation = the eye block's camera_optical <- camera_link times the hand-eye fit camera_link <- chip (a neck sweep, gyro vs encoder rates, Kabsch; scratch/head_imu_handeye.py), checked by gravity at rest in camera_link to 0.75 deg (scratch/vio_night/gravity_check.py); the first nominal (a pure axis permutation onto the optical axes) skipped the eye block and sat 3.6 deg off. Offset by eye 0.03/-0.035/-0.02 m (Kalibr pending); time_offset_s (t_imu = t_cam + shift, Kalibr's sign) from the pictures' own motion (phase correlation of consecutive frames) against the gyro over slow pans and tilts, -92/-95 ms in two runs, under camera_stamp grab and AUTO exposure at night: the grab stamp sits ~93 ms after the exposure, and this moves with the exposure (scratch/vio_night/cam_imu_lag.py)
head_imu.note: chip axes against the rectified left eye's optical frame, from the photo

notes: The lens is measured: ros/calibrate.sh (45 views of a 9x6 checkerboard, rms 0.23 px, 2026-09-13) wrote the intrinsics block and set calibrated: true, and pepin.camera.optics answers from it. hfov_deg is the nominal pinhole that reader falls back to when calibrated is false — it is 82.94, the field of view the calibration measured, because the best known number is what a bad calibration must be switched off onto; it was 78.0, the lidar-beam fit of 2026-09-10, and 70 is the vendor number that put the image edges 8 deg wrong. The mount beside it is measured too: the pitch from the level frames and the encoder, the height from a tape (see the mount note). The 78 / 26 self-calibration is STALE and is not the source of any number in this file any more. WHICH camera the robot's head is, is the top-level "active" above: every node that reads this file asks pepin.camera for the active one, and PEPIN_CAMERA in a node's environment overrides it (ros/laptop.sh forwards it into the container). The board's own half of the switch is /etc/default/pepin-camera (board/pepin-camera.service): the device and the resolution ustreamer serves. The two must agree — "active": "stereo" beside a board still streaming 1280x720 mono is a node splitting a webcam picture down the middle.
